data.raw_response:
=== Morphological Assessment Form ===
A. Leaf Arrangement & Architecture
    1. Leaf relative position (alternate / opposite / whorled): whorled (multiple leaves clearly attached at the same node in a circular arrangement, typically 5-7 leaves per whorl)
    2. Leaf spacing (clustered / distal): clustered (whorls of leaves are closely spaced along the stem)
B. Leaf Complexity
    3. Leaf complexity (simple / compound): simple (each leaf unit is a single blade without leaflet division)
    4. Compound leaf type, ONLY if leaf complexity is compound (odd-pinnate / even-pinnate): N/A
    5. Number of leaflets (integer estimate 2, 4, 8, …): N/A
    6. Leaflet arrangement (opposite / alternate / subopposite): N/A
C. Leaf Morphology
    7. Leaf margin (entire / toothed) AND if toothed (dentate, serrate, etc.)): entire (margins are smooth without teeth)
    8. Leaf shape (elliptic, obovate, lanceolate, etc.): obovate to elliptic (leaf is broader towards the apex and tapers towards the base)
    9. Leaf apex (acute, obtuse, acuminate): acute (tapering to a distinct point)
    10. Leaf base (rounded, cordate, cuneate): cuneate to attenuate (tapering gradually towards the petiole attachment)
    11. Venation type (pinnate / palmate / parallel): pinnate (single midrib with secondary veins branching from it)
    12. Secondary veins (visibility, spacing, number): visible and prominent, appearing to curve towards the leaf margin (intramarginal)
    13. Leaf surface features (glabrous, shiny, dull, rugose): shiny and glabrous (smooth and reflecting light, indicating a glossy surface)
    14. Leaf surface trichomes (present / absent): absent (no visible hairs on the leaf surface)
    15. Petiole length (short / long): short (petioles are relatively short compared to the leaf blade)
    16. Petiole features (winged / grooved / terete): terete (cylindrical in cross-section)
D. Stem & Shoot Traits
    17. Stem type, may not be visible (woody / herbaceous): woody (the main stem appears rigid and dark, characteristic of a woody seedling)
    18. Stem trichomes (present / absent): absent (stem appears smooth without visible hairs)
    19. Stem color: dark brown to blackish (visible in the lower stem and petioles)
    20. Stem texture (smooth / ridged / lenticellate): smooth (no obvious ridges or lenticels visible)
E. Other Visible Seedling Traits
    21. Stipules, sometimes visible only in close-up images (present / absent): unclear (stipules are not clearly visible at the nodes)
    22. Latex, rarely visible but extremely diagnostic when present (present / not observed): not observed (no latex exudate visible)
    23. Pulvinus, for Fabaceae family only (present / absent): absent (no pulvinus joint visible at the base of the leaf)
    24. Tendrils (present / absent): absent (no tendrils visible)
F. Notes: The leaves show some minor damage in the form of small holes. The overall appearance is of a healthy, young woody seedling with distinct whorled phyllotaxy.
